Worum geht es?

Wenn in der Schweiz eine Feuerwehr alarmiert wird, läuft die Meldung mit hoher Wahrscheinlichkeit über unsere Systeme. Rund 400 Feuerwehren in 16 Kantonen arbeiten mit unseren Lösungen, von der Alarmierung über die Einsatzführung bis zur Einsatzplanung.

Das heisst: Unsere Software muss funktionieren, auch nachts um 3 Uhr. Diese Verantwortung prägt, wie wir entwickeln.

Wir suchen dich als Software Engineer, der unsere Plattform mitträgt. Nicht als weitere Person im Team, sondern als eine tragende Säule in unserem Team.

Über uns

Die EvoSys AG wurde 2011 gegründet und entwickelt seit 2016 eigene Software für Behörden und Organisationen für Rettung und Sicherheit (BORS). Wir sind ein inhabergeführtes Familienunternehmen in Thun mit 9 Mitarbeitenden und in unserem Markt führend.

Unsere Produkte heissen AlarmHub, Intervento, FloriPlan, AlarmDisplay und SpotPilot. Sie decken den ganzen Ablauf ab, von der Alarmierung bis zur Auswertung nach dem Einsatz. 2028 kommt mit Respondo eine weitere Lösung dazu.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst unsere bestehenden Plattformen weiter und setzt neue Funktionen von der Idee bis in den Betrieb um.

  • Du prägst unsere Architektur mit. Unsere Kundenbasis wächst stark, und unsere Systeme müssen mitwachsen. Konkret bereiten wir den Schritt auf Kubernetes vor und bauen Dienste so um, dass sie zuverlässig skalieren.

  • Du arbeitest an Schnittstellen zu Einsatzzentralen, Partnersystemen und Behördenplattformen.

  • Du setzt KI-gestützte Werkzeuge im Entwicklungsalltag ein, so wie wir alle.

  • Du nimmst an Code Reviews teil und trägst zu Qualität und Dokumentation bei.

  • Du unterstützt bei anspruchsvollen technischen Fragen aus dem Betrieb.

Perspektive

Mit der Zeit kannst du die fachliche Verantwortung für einen Produktbereich übernehmen. Und wenn es für beide Seiten passt, ist längerfristig auch eine technische Führungsrolle denkbar. Solche Rollen besetzen wir aus dem Team heraus. Voraussetzung für diese Stelle ist das aber ausdrücklich nicht.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Rund 2 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Entwicklung von Webanwendungen. Die ersten Jahre hast du hinter dir und arbeitest selbständig, ohne enge Begleitung.

About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role

Every airframe Harmattan AI flies starts with a model. System identification turns flight data into the verified dynamics that guidance and control are designed, tuned and trained on. It is the foundation of an autopilot that adapts across multirotors, fixed wings, VTOLs and missiles.

As a System Identification Engineer, working out of Lausanne, you will own the path from flight test to identified model. You will design and run your own experiments, build a repeatable identification pipeline, and deliver models the G&C team can trust.

 
 

Responsibilities

  • Experiment Design & Flight Test: Plan and run your own identification tests, from excitation design to flight tests, including coordinating with the .

  • Model Identification: Identify rigid-body, aerodynamic, propulsion and actuator dynamics using frequency and time-domain methods, including closed-loop identification on vehicles flown under a controller.

  • Propulsion & Actuators: Characterize motors, ESCs, propellers and control surfaces, including bandwidth, delays, saturation, and thermal and battery effects.

  • Identification Pipeline: Build and maintain an automated, reproducible pipeline from flight logs to identified model. This covers ingestion, data-quality checks, estimation, validation and reporting.

  • Model Validation: Validate models against held-out flight data, quantify uncertainty, and make sure each model is fit for purpose: controller design, simulation, or training learned G&C.

  • New Airframes: Extend the capability from multirotors to control-surface multirotors, fixed wings, tail-sitters and missiles.

  • Simulation & G&C Support: Deliver models into simulation, SITL and HITL, and work closely with control, guidance and embedded engineers to close the loop between models and flight results.

  • Mentorship: Depending on seniority, support the team by mentoring junior engineers and interns.

 
 

Candidate Requirements

  • Educational Background: A strong academic record with a degree in aerospace, control, mechanical engineering or a related STEM field. A practical track record matters more than the specific degree.

  • System Identification: Proven experience identifying dynamic models of flying platforms from real data, in both the frequency and time domain, including the pitfalls of closed-loop data.

  • Flight Mechanics & Control: Solid grasp of rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamic forces and moments, non-dimensionalization, stability modes and propulsion models. Also enough control background to know what the model will be used for.

  • Flight Testing: Hands-on experience planning and running flight tests and working from raw, imperfect logs.

  • Software: Strong Python and scientific computing skills, with the discipline to build tools others can rerun.

 

Nice to have

  • Rigorous about data quality, uncertainty and validation; skeptical of models until they are proven.

  • Autonomous and hands-on, comfortable moving between bench, field and code.

  • Communicates clearly, able to present models and test results to engineers and senior stakeholders.

  • Thrives under pressure in a fast-paced environment with a no-task-is-too-small mentality.

  • Fixed-wing aerodynamic modeling; VTOL or tail-sitter dynamics; remote pilot certification; experience with real flight logs; structural or vibration modes; data-driven or learned dynamics models.

  • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission of providing a defensive edge to allied nations through ethical, high-impact technology.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to shape the electrical architecture of a first-of-a-kind power plant and define how it interacts with both internal consumers and the wider electrical grid. You will drive the modernization of power system monitoring, diagnostics, and predictive maintenance strategies, leveraging data and digital technologies to improve reliability and operational performance. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. Join the Wingtra team and become part of this venture-backed robotics scaleup with a global and international team of 125+ dedicated Wingtranauts who want to see their actions have a positive and lasting impact on the world. Founded more than 8 years ago at ETH Zurich, Europe’s leading robotics university, our goal is to build the best aerial robots to digitize the world at the push of a button and set the basis for faster and better decisions. Wingtra provides efficient and reliable data solutions to a variety of industries ranging from mining, construction and agriculture to humanitarian organizations, environmentalists and wildlife monitoring groups.

We are reaching for the stars and together we might just get there. Open communication, asking hard questions and valuing diverse viewpoints are but a few things that will help us achieve our goals. Above all we will never stop learning and striving to help each other reach our maximum potential.

Help us take Wingtra’s new product platforms from fast prototypes to reliable series production. Embedded in the engineering team, you own mechanical design, qualification and industrialization through initial ramp-up. Together we deliver a qualified product, a complete product file and a working production line. We are early adopters of AI and actively build agentic workflows across engineering, from design and test planning to execution and analysis.

Responsibilities

  • Take a new aircraft from concept to series production. You work in a small team with electronics designers and test engineers. You get direct feedback from prototypes, flight tests and production builds.

  • Design and iterate lightweight parts. You design, build and test parts and assemblies, then improve them until they are ready for production.

  • Choose materials and processes with care. You balance performance, volumes, unit cost, tooling investment and lead times.

  • Own DFX. You design for manufacturing, assembly, quality, cost and serviceability, and you settle tolerances, interfaces and process constraints early.

  • Work hand in hand with suppliers. You partner with sourcing on technical feasibility, tooling and part iterations.

  • Own qualification. You qualify parts with the intended production materials and processes, and you agree product-specific acceptance criteria with the test engineers.

  • Deliver the production-ready product file. CAD, 2D drawings, tolerances, BOMs, material and process specifications and acceptance criteria.

  • Hand over a running line. Once the qualification gates have passed and ramp-up is complete, you hand the line and the product file to Production and Production Engineering.


    • Requirements

  • You have several years of experience taking mechanical products through the full lifecycle: prototype, series production and quality monitoring at the customer. Ideally on structurally critical products at volumes of hundreds to a few thousand units.

  • You are strong in CAD (Solidworks/PDM preferred), tolerance analysis and material selection.

  • You have practical experience with injection molding as well as additive manufacturing for functional plastic parts.

  • You prototype fast and pragmatically, then qualify and document with discipline.

  • You like hands-on work: builds, testing and working with suppliers.

  • You use AI for design exploration, qualification planning and data analysis. You check its output, share new workflows and keep raising the team’s bar.

  • You are curious, flexible and collaborative, with a real drive to build the next great thing.

    • If you enjoy teamwork more than being the individual superhero, and if you thrive in a feedback-driven culture and an exciting, unconventional yet structured and progressive start-up environment, we would love to hear from you.

🍇 About grape: 
 
Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Recognising the need for innovation in the traditional employee insurance model we are set to revolutionize the employee insurance industry. We help companies support people before and after they get sick and to make more of their time. Our insurance solutions reduce monotonous and manual work for employees, doctors, HR & payroll managers. As we strive to lead a technology-driven transformation, we put employees first.
 
At grape we pride ourselves on our people and our culture. We continue to grow fast and that’s where you come in. Our team is dynamic, diverse and full of creative ideas. Want to join? We can’t wait to get to know you!

Your role

As Head of Insurance Supply, you will own grape’s carrier and reinsurance partnerships. You will build and diversify our capacity panel, secure the structures behind existing and new products, and ensure our insurance supply grows with the business.

Today, this responsibility is led by our CEOs. You will take it over, build it into a dedicated function and represent Insurance Supply as a member of grape’s Leadership Team.


What you’ll do:

1. Build and diversify our capacity panel

  • Develop grape’s capacity strategy for Switzerland and Liechtenstein.
  • Identify, qualify, negotiate with and onboard new carriers and reinsurers.
  • Lead relationships from the first conversation through due diligence, commercial negotiation and signed agreement.
  • Secure the contracted capacity required for grape’s annual business plan and written commitments for the following year.
  • Diversify the panel to support growth, enable new products and reduce concentration risk.

    •  

    2. Build strong carrier partnerships

  • Own carrier and reinsurer relationships at operational, commercial and executive level.
  • Establish a clear governance cadence, including operational reviews, strategic meetings and annual capacity negotiations.
  • Own commercial terms, contracts, renewals, outsourcing agreements and service levels.
  • Monitor partnership performance, resolve issues early and build relationships that grow over time.
  • Represent grape credibly across the insurance, reinsurance and broking market.

    •  

    3. Shape products and build the function

  • Design and secure the carrier and reinsurance structures required for new products.
  • Evaluate pricing, loss ratios, reserving, commissions, capital requirements and solvency implications.
  • Work closely with Actuarial, Underwriting, Legal, Compliance, Risk, Product and Distribution.
  • Own the Insurance Supply strategy, priorities, OKRs, processes and reporting.
  • Provide the Leadership Team with a clear view of capacity coverage, pipeline and risk.

  • Strong commercial judgement and the confidence to negotiate with senior stakeholders across carriers, reinsurers, MGAs and brokers.
  • A strong understanding of insurance portfolio economics, including loss ratios, reserving, pricing, capacity and capital implications.
  • Experience building long-term external partnerships and a relevant network across the carrier, reinsurance or broking market.
  • The ability to move between strategy, relationship building, negotiation and operational detail.
  • Fluent English.

    • Strong advantage:
  • Experience working within an MGA or directly with MGA and programme structures.
  • Knowledge of Swiss and Liechtenstein employee insurance, particularly KTG, UVG and UVG-Z.
  • Familiarity with the Swiss and Liechtenstein regulatory environment.
  • German or French proficiency.

data.description:
Über VIA HealthTech

VIA macht aus einer Therapiesitzung ein fertiges Sitzungsprotokoll und aus Sitzungsprotokollen vollständige psychologische Berichte. Arbeit, die Therapeut:innen bisher mehrere Stunden pro Woche gekostet hat.

Wir sind die marktführende KI-Assistenz für Psychotherapeut:innen. Über 4.000 Psychotherapeut:innen im DACH-Raum nutzen VIA, wir verarbeiten Hunderttausende Sitzungen pro Monat. Wir sind nach ISO 27001:2022 zertifiziert und verfügen über ein BSI-C5-Testat.

Wir sind ein multidisziplinäres Team in Berlin-Mitte. Marktführer in Deutschland zu sein, ist erst der Startpunkt. Die Schweiz ist unser nächster Markt, und du baust ihn mit auf.

Die Rolle

Du bist unsere erste Person im Schweizer Markt. Du baust die Pipeline von Grund auf, entwickelst das Playbook und führst es selbst aus.

In Deutschland läuft unser Funnel vor allem über Webinare: Therapeut:innen melden sich an, testen VIA 14 Tage und buchen selbst. Du findest heraus, was davon in der Schweiz funktioniert und was anders laufen muss: Qualifizierung am Telefon, Cold-Calling, andere Outbound- und Inbound-Kanäle, Verbände, Weiterbildungsinstitute, grössere Organisationen als eigener Kanal. Du testest, misst und skalierst, wo der Hebel am grössten ist.

Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing an Zielgruppen, Kampagnen und Botschaften für den Schweizer Markt und gibst direkt zurück, was im Gespräch wirklich zieht.

Die Rolle ist senior gedacht. Wenn du mid-level, aber aussergewöhnlich schnell und hungrig bist, bewirb dich trotzdem.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Den Markt öffnen. Du identifizierst die wichtigsten Zielgruppen in der Schweiz: selbstständige psychologische Psychotherapeut:innen, Psychiater:innen, Organisationen der psychologischen Psychotherapie, Ambulatorien und Kliniken. Du priorisierst, wo wir zuerst gewinnen.
  • Leads in Kund:innen verwandeln. Qualifizierungsgespräche, Webinare, Demos, Follow-up während der Testphase, Abschluss. Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Schweizer Kund:innen.
  • Neue Kanäle erschliessen. Berufsverbände wie FSP, ASP und SBAP, Weiterbildungsinstitute, Fachveranstaltungen und Kongresse. Erstansprache per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn, wo sie sich lohnt.
  • Playbook bauen, während du verkaufst. Was konvertiert, welche Einwände in der Schweiz wirklich kommen (etwa zu Datenschutz und Datenhaltung), welche Sequenz funktioniert.
  • Zahlen verantworten. Deine KPIs entlang des Funnels, gemeinsam mit unserem Commercial Engine Lead, der Tracking und Infrastruktur baut.
  • Sales-Enablement-Material. Du passt an, was zum Verkaufen und Vermarkten in der Schweiz am besten wirkt, von Sprache bis Preisdarstellung in CHF.
  • Feedback ins Produkt bringen. Was Schweizer Kund:innen brauchen und woran Deals scheitern, besprichst du direkt mit dem Produktteam.

Dein Profil

Must-have

  • Nachgewiesene Abschlüsse im B2B-Vertrieb in der Schweiz, idealerweise SaaS oder Digital Health, belegbar in Zahlen
  • Echte Hunter-Mentalität. Du hast bereits aktiv Erstkontakte am Telefon gemacht und hast damit kein Problem. Wenn dich 40 Gespräche am Tag abschrecken, ist das die falsche Rolle
  • Kenntnis des Schweizer Gesundheitswesens oder die Fähigkeit, dich sehr schnell einzuarbeiten: Grundversicherung, Anordnungsmodell, Rolle von Kantonen und Verbänden
  • Glaubwürdigkeit gegenüber Therapeut:innen. Psychotherapeut:innen vertrauen vor allem Psychotherapeut:innen. Entweder bringst du diesen Hintergrund mit, oder du arbeitest dich so schnell und so tief ein, dass man es dir im Gespräch nicht anmerkt
  • Systemdenken. Du baust reproduzierbare Prozesse statt Einzelfälle, mit dem Ziel, dass dein Ansatz auch ohne dich funktioniert
  • Hunger und unternehmerischer Ehrgeiz. Du willst einen neuen Markt aufbauen, nicht eine Quote abarbeiten
  • Kommunikationsstärke mit Abschlussfokus. Empathisch und auf Augenhöhe, denn Psychotherapeut:innen merken sofort, wenn jemand verkauft, statt zu verstehen
  • Selbstständige, strukturierte und datengetriebene Arbeitsweise, auch remote und ohne Team vor Ort, sowie sicherer Umgang mit CRM-Systemen
  • Deutsch auf verhandlungssicherem Niveau (C2), auch Schweizerdeutsch, gutes Englisch
  • Verfügbarkeit am frühen Abend. Unsere Zielgruppe ist häufig erst nach der letzten Sitzung erreichbar, Termine zwischen 17 und 19 Uhr gehören dazu. Im Gegenzug gestaltest du deinen Tag frei

Von Vorteil

  • Französisch und/oder Italienisch, um später auch die weiteren Gebiete anzusprechen

This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here

The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.

What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.

What you'll do

You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.

  • Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

  • Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

  • Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

  • Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

  • Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

  • Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

  • You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

  • At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

  • You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

  • You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both

  • You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data

  • You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls

  • You make things simpler over time, not more clever

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home

  • You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you

  • You want a well-defined backlog handed to you

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount

Our stack

Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

  • Remote within the EU or EEA

  • Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

  • Competitive compensation

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here

Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.

We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

What you'll own

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

  • Training and fine-tuning: embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

  • Document understanding: models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

  • Product matching: retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

  • Evaluation: offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

  • Training and serving infrastructure: automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

  • Customer problems: when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next.

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

  • A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

  • Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

  • You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

  • You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

  • You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

  • You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

  • You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure.

  • You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you.

  • You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is.

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title.

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going.

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls.

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home.

  • You don't like talking to customers.

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you.

  • You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you.

  • You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug.

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount.

Our stack

Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

data.description:
For this role, we will only consider candidates who are currently based in the Netherlands.

About SkinVision

Skin cancer is highly treatable when caught early, but limited access to specialist care and long wait times delay diagnosis, increasing the risk of late-stage cases and driving up treatment costs. SkinVision, founded in Amsterdam in 2012, exists to close that gap. Our proprietary AI — certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU regulation, with over 90% sensitivity and 89% specificity — has already helped nearly 3 million people worldwide detect early signs of skin cancer. Today, SkinVision has a database of more than 6 million skin spot assessments and can reach 20 million people through insurer partnerships. High-risk cases are reviewed by a team of dermatologists, who support users in taking the right next step — from urgent care to a specialist referral. We are extending this further, connecting users faster to the specialist care they need. We're a focused, international team, active globally, united by one goal: making early detection accessible to everyone, everywhere. If you join us, you're not just building a product — you're helping close the gap between a person noticing something and getting the care they need.

DevOps at SkinVision

As a DevOps Engineer at SkinVision, you will play a key role in building, scaling, and securing the infrastructure that powers our AI-driven health platform. You’ll design and maintain our cloud-based systems in AWS, implement CI/CD pipelines, enhance observability using Datadog, and drive operational excellence through automation and monitoring.

Your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of a medical-grade system that serves users globally. You’ll collaborate closely with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure smooth delivery, rapid deployments, and resilient operations — ultimately enabling us to deliver life-saving technology with confidence.

Beyond hands-on expertise with AWS and modern DevOps tooling, we’re looking for someone who thinks architecturally. You’ll get to know our current setup, form your own view of how it should evolve, and help define a target vision for our infrastructure, then drive its implementation. Day-to-day operational work is part of the role, but we value someone who thinks before building and takes ownership of where our infrastructure goes next.

What you will do

Cloud Infrastructure & Automation

  • Design, build, and manage AWS-based infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency.

  • Implement and manage infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation.

  • Automate environment provisioning, configuration, and deployments using CI/CD pipelines.

  • Ensure system resilience, security, and performance through automated monitoring and alerting.

CI/CD & Deployment

  • Design and optimize CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, reliable, and safe deployments across environments.

  • Manage deployment workflows using Argo CD and Kubernetes.

  • Collaborate with developers and ML engineers to streamline build, test, and release processes.

  • Integrate automated testing, rollback strategies, and version control into the deployment lifecycle.

Observability & Monitoring

  • Build a comprehensive observability stack using Datadog for metrics, logs, traces, and alerts.

  • Define service-level objectives (SLOs), service-level indicators (SLIs), and dashboards for system performance.

  • Proactively detect and resolve performance bottlenecks, capacity issues, and reliability risks.

  • Create automated health checks and ensure visibility across production systems.

Security & Compliance

  • Implement security best practices for AWS, containers, and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Manage identity, access, and secret handling (IAM, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store).

  • Ensure compliance with medical device standards and data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA).

  • Partner with the Information Security Officer to embed security controls across infrastructure and deployments.

Reliability & Incident Management

  • Lead incident response and root cause analysis for infrastructure or deployment-related issues.

  • Establish SLAs and operational runbooks for production environments.

  • Continuously improve system reliability through chaos testing, redundancy, and fault tolerance.

  • Mentor engineers on DevOps principles, observability practices, and infrastructure automation.

Infrastructure Strategy & Architecture

  • Assess the current infrastructure and deployment setup, and form a well-reasoned view of how it should evolve.

  • Define and maintain a target architecture for our cloud platform, balancing reliability, scalability, security, and cost.

  • Translate the target vision into a practical roadmap and drive its implementation incrementally, alongside day-to-day operations.

  • Document and communicate architectural decisions, aligning with engineering and leadership on technical direction.


Essential skills

  • Minimum of 6 years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Infrastructure roles.

  • Strong expertise with AWS services (EC2, ECS/EKS, S3, RDS, CloudWatch, Lambda, etc.).

  • Expert in Kubernetes and Argo CD, deploying and managing production-grade custom Helm charts with secure, automated GitOps workflows in EKS

  • Advanced knowledge of CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar).

  • Proficiency in Datadog for observability, monitoring, and alerting.

  • Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, Bash, or Go.

  • Experience managing infrastructure with Terraform, CloudFormation, or Ansible.

  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals, load balancing, and API gateway configuration.

  • Excellent problem-solving and incident management skills.

Desirable skills

  • Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, MedTech, or FinTech.

  • Familiarity with multi-environment architecture (staging, pre-prod, production) and blue-green deployments.

  • Exposure to event-driven systems, message queues, and data streaming (Kafka, SNS/SQS).

  • Understanding of Zero Trust networking and cloud security best practices.

  • Experience in cost optimization and performance tuning in AWS.

Qualifications

  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

  • Certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), or Terraform Associate are a plus.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary, additional benefits, and a hybrid working policy

  • A vibrant, dynamic, and rapidly growing scale-up in Amsterdam

  • An enthusiastic, professional, and international team

  • Regular team events, including off-sites and fun activities

  • Unlimited skin checks for you

Beyond optimizing existing channels, you'll explore, launch, and scale new acquisition opportunities, including those emerging from the changing AI- and LLM-driven marketing landscape.

Most importantly, this is a hands-on role where you'll do more than develop strategies and bring ideas to the table. You'll actively execute initiatives yourself or work closely with the wider team to bring them to life. Whether you're launching a new campaign, testing an acquisition channel, or improving conversion, you'll take ownership of turning opportunities into measurable business results.


On a typical week

It's Monday morning, and you start the week with a coffee and a look at last week's acquisition performance. You open GA4, HubSpot, and your marketing dashboards to see how we're tracking against our B2C and B2B MQL targets. While digging into the data, you notice that one of our paid campaigns is generating plenty of traffic, but conversions have dropped. You investigate further, identify a few potential causes, and head into the Growth Marketing stand-up with some ideas to improve performance.

After the stand-up, you catch up with our Performance Marketing Specialist to review campaign performance and discuss opportunities to scale. You identify a promising new audience and agree to test a different creative approach. Rather than just handing over your ideas, you jump into the advertising platform to help set up the campaign and work with the team to get the new creatives ready for launch.

On Tuesday, you're focused on improving our B2B acquisition funnel. You've spotted an opportunity to increase conversions on the AI for HR Boot Camp landing page. You meet with our B2B Marketer and CRO Specialist to review the data, discuss your hypothesis, and agree on an experiment. You brief the team, align with sales on the proposed changes, and help move the experiment towards launch.

Wednesday is a work-from-home day, giving you time to dive deeper into our acquisition strategy. You've been exploring how AI and LLMs are changing the way HR professionals discover training providers. You identify a potential new acquisition opportunity, research the market, and put together a practical plan to test it. Later, you meet with the Head of Growth Marketing to challenge your assumptions, refine the approach, and agree on the next steps.

On Thursday, you review the performance of our B2C email nurture flows with the Email Marketing team. You notice an opportunity to improve conversions from leads to MQLs and propose a change to the messaging and sequence. After lunch with colleagues in the office, you turn your attention to an upcoming quarterly campaign, working with the wider Marketing team to finalize the messaging and coordinate the launch. You also start investigating new channels that could help expand the campaign's reach and attract new audiences.

Friday starts with reviewing the results of a recent landing page experiment. The changes have improved conversion, so you work with the CRO Specialist to roll them out more broadly. You also catch up with our BizOps team to improve HubSpot reporting, ensuring we have better visibility into acquisition performance and opportunities for growth. Before wrapping up the week, you review progress against our growth priorities, share your findings with the team, and identify the next opportunities worth pursuing.

After a productive week of analyzing, experimenting, and driving initiatives forward, you close your laptop and join your colleagues for Friday drinks.

Who you are

We're looking for an ambitious, data-driven, and commercially minded growth marketer with an entrepreneurial spirit. Someone who loves identifying opportunities, challenging existing approaches, and turning ideas into measurable results. About Shiftbase

At Shiftbase, we build workforce software that helps people get work done. Thousands of teams across Europe rely on our platform every day to plan work, track time, and manage leave, freeing them from unnecessary admin so they can focus on what matters and what sparked their business.

As we continue to grow in customers, usage and product ambition, the demands on our platform grow with us. Our backend needs to scale in quality, reliability and speed of change. That’s why we’re investing heavily in modernising our platform, building a foundation that allows us to move faster, deliver better experiences, and support the next phase of Shiftbase’s growth.

About the role:


As a Senior Backend Engineer, you are a key driver of both product delivery and platform modernisation. You work on the core of our backend, improving reliability, performance and scalability, with the explicit goal of turning Shiftbase from a platform people enjoy into a platform they love.

You help evolve a mature monolithic codebase into a more modular, testable and future-proof architecture. By modernising the foundation of the product, you directly enable better user experiences, faster iteration and higher overall product quality.

What you'll do

Drive technical excellence

  • Design and deliver high-quality, scalable solutions for complex features and system components

  • Make informed architectural decisions that balance pragmatism with long-term vision

  • Set the bar for technical craft through your contributions and code reviews

  • Own complex technical initiatives from design through production, breaking them into testable increments

Build for reliability and scale

  • Define comprehensive testing strategies for complex features, championing quality within the team

  • Debug and resolve complex issues across multiple components, improving system observability

  • Apply security best practices throughout the development lifecycle

  • Contribute to monitoring, alerting and system health improvements

Enable team growth

  • Mentor engineers with targeted technical guidance and feedback

  • Support onboarding and enable a collaborative, knowledge-sharing environment

  • Help shape delivery practices and improve team velocity through data-informed decisions


What we're looking for

Core technical expertise

You have deep backend engineering experience with complex, high-scale systems. We don't expect expertise in everything listed below. We value engineers who've built depth and breadth through genuine curiosity and a drive to solve real problems. These are examples of competencies that matter in this role:

  • Modern PHP & architectural patterns: Experience with hexagonal architecture, domain-driven design, or similar patterns that emphasize domain modeling over framework magic. You can build maintainable systems without relying on framework shortcuts.

  • SQL & database design: Comfort writing raw SQL (not just ORM abstractions) and working with complex relational schemas particularly around time-sensitive data like scheduling, timesheets and payroll where integrity and performance are critical.

  • Legacy modernisation experience: You've gradually evolved mature systems rather than pursuing big-bang rewrites. You know when to modernize strategically vs. leaving working code untouched, and understand the balance between progress and stability when serving thousands of customers.

  • Monolith to services: Experience breaking down monoliths with good judgment about when distribution solves real problems (deployment bottlenecks, team autonomy) vs. when it adds unnecessary complexity.

  • Testing in legacy contexts: Practical experience with unit and integration testing, particularly incrementally improving coverage in existing systems.

This might be your dream job if…

✅ You enjoy modernising a mature platform and turning legacy code into something you’re proud of

✅ You get energy from breaking down a monolith and shaping a more modular, service-oriented architecture

✅ You care about product quality, not just “shipping code”.

✅ You like improving reliability, performance and developer experience as much as adding new features

✅ You enjoy working closely with product and frontend to make better technical and product decisions

This probably isn’t your dream job if…

⛔️ You only want to work on greenfield projects and avoid legacy systems altogether

⛔️ You’re uncomfortable refactoring existing code or making incremental improvements

⛔️ You prefer being handed fully-defined solutions rather than helping shape them

⛔️ You’re looking for a role where architecture decisions are already “done”

⛔️ You’d rather optimise locally than care about the end-to-end product experience

Note: Candidates outside the Netherlands will not be considered

Ben jij die nieuwsgierige onderzoeker die energie krijgt van data, duurzaamheid en nieuwe inzichten?
Wil jij een inhoudelijke bijdrage leveren aan de statistieken van het CBS?

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het kabinet wil dat Nederland in 2050 volledig circulair is. Om te kunnen volgen of we die doelstelling halen, is betrouwbare informatie nodig over onder andere afval en emissies naar water. Het CBS verzamelt en publiceert deze gegevens voor bedrijven. Daarbij maken we vooral gebruik van gegevens uit het elektronisch Milieujaarverslag (e-MJV), aangevuld met enquêtes.

Naast de hoeveelheid afval en wateremissies brengen we ook de milieukosten van bedrijven in kaart, bijvoorbeeld de kosten voor afvalverwerking en voor het lozen van afvalwater. Hiervoor wordt nu een aparte enquête gebruikt. Maar is dat eigenlijk wel nodig?

Tijdens je stage onderzoek je of we de milieukosten voor afval en wateremissies kunnen berekenen met gegevens die al beschikbaar zijn. Je combineert bijvoorbeeld gegevens over de hoeveelheid afval en geloosd water met bestaande indicatoren, zoals gemiddelde kosten per ton afval en sectorspecifieke kosten per kubieke meter geloosd water.

Je gaat onder andere:

  • bestaande data en indicatoren analyseren en beoordelen op bruikbaarheid;

  • onderzoeken welke methode het meest geschikt is om de milieukosten te schatten;

  • een berekening of model ontwikkelen waarmee de kosten kunnen worden afgeleid;

  • de uitkomsten vergelijken met de beschikbare gegevens uit de huidige enquête;

  • onderzoeken hoe betrouwbaar en bruikbaar de schattingen zijn;

  • je bevindingen vertalen naar een concreet advies voor het CBS.

Met jouw onderzoek willen we bepalen of we meer uit bestaande data kunnen halen en minder hoeven uit te vragen bij bedrijven. Als blijkt dat de milieukosten betrouwbaar kunnen worden berekend, kunnen de uitkomsten bovendien worden gebruikt om de bestaande afval- en waterstatistieken te controleren.

In het meest gunstige scenario kan de aparte enquête naar milieukosten gedeeltelijk of helemaal vervallen. Dat betekent minder administratieve lasten voor bedrijven, efficiënter gebruik van beschikbare data en mogelijk betrouwbaardere statistieken.

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Den Haag

We verwelkomen je binnen de sector Leefomgeving bij team Milieu. Met 20 gedreven professionals werken we aan milieu gerelateerde statistieken en doen we onderzoek naar actuele thema’s zoals klimaat(verandering) en circulaire economie. We werken nauw samen met andere teams binnen het CBS.

We werken hard aan het continu verbeteren van onze statistieken en de cijfers beschikbaar te stellen voor het publiek. Voorbeelden van recente publicaties uit ons team zijn:

  • Bedrijven investeerden in 2024 minder in milieu | CBS

  • Bijna 2 procent meer bedrijfs- en industrieafval in 2021 | CBS

  • Milieukosten en -investeringen van bedrijven | CBS

Dit breng jij mee

Je volgt een wo-opleiding milieukunde, economie, technische bestuurskunde, data science of een aanverwante opleiding.

  • Je hebt affiniteit met het onderwerp circulaire economie.

  • Je bent analytisch sterk en kunt complexe vraagstukken gestructureerd onderzoeken en vertalen naar heldere inzichten.

  • Je kunt goed programmeren in R.

  • Je bent sociaal en communicatief vaardig en kunt je ideeën en bevindingen helder overbrengen aan verschillende gesprekspartners.

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk.

Dit kun je van ons verwachten

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je:

  • jouw competenties in kwantitatieve data-analyse versterkt door gebruik te maken van milieustatistieken en economische databronnen;

  • jouw onderzoeksvaardigheden aanscherpt op het gebied van de circulaire economie en levenscyclusanalyse;

  • jouw programmeervaardigheden in R verder ontwikkelt;

  • ervaring opdoet met het interpreteren van verschillende datasets om betrouwbare profielen op te stellen.

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800 bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week).

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken.

Dit zijn onze voorwaarden

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken.
Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking.

Job Summary

The Engineering Manager, Mammography leads the engineering team behind Mammo Dx, DeepHealth's FDA- and CE-cleared breast cancer detection AI for 2D mammography and 3D tomosynthesis, within the Clinical AI organization that brings together engineering, AI, clinical, and regulatory teams across the US and Europe. The role also acts as Technical Delivery Manager for the team, owning delivery of every release from plan to production. Working with the Mammo product lead, QRC, and US teams, the Engineering Manager, Mammography ensures the right software reaches the right sites on time, with the quality a medical device requires. The role reports to the Software Engineering Manager, Clinical AI Devices.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead and mentor a team of 3 to 4 engineers; support their technical and professional growth.

  • Set clear goals, run regular 1:1s and performance reviews, and give constructive feedback.

  • Recruit, onboard and retain great engineers.

  • Foster a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement.

Release & Delivery Management (TDM)

  • Own the Mammo release plan jointly with the product lead: scope, sizing, milestones and monthly release tracking.

  • Drive each release end to end: planning, development, verification, regulatory sign-off, deployment and post-release follow-up.

  • Align the Mammo team's delivery practices, processes and tools with the Clinical AI standards.

  • Make sure test setups are ready so product can run functional validation on time.

  • Contribute to the 3- and 6-month roadmap rituals and keep delivery commitments predictable.

Quality & Regulatory Compliance

  • Work with QRC on regulatory impact assessments for every change.

Cross-Functional & US Collaboration

  • Communicate status, risks and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Coordinate with platform, AI and data teams on dependencies.

Technical Leadership

Take part in design and architecture reviews, challenge estimates and unblock the team.

Keep a strong grasp of the system without writing production code day to day.

PLEASE NOTE: This is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and requirements of the position described above. Other functions may be assigned and management retains the right to add or change duties at any time.


Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience

GRESB is the global sustainability intelligence standard for real assets. For over 15 years, real estate and infrastructure managers have reported to us, building a dataset of 150,000+ assets across more than 2,000 portfolios. Together with Asset Impact, which tracks emissions for over 300,000 physical assets and 77,000 companies, we’re turning that data into decision-grade intelligence for investors, lenders, index providers and regulators.

We’re building a new Client & Data Intelligence organization to showcase the value of the data to investors and develop new use cases within the ecosystem. It brings sales, product and data teams together under one leader, the Chief Client & Data Intelligence Officer. This role is the person who makes that organization run. The role is based out of Amsterdam.

The Role

You’ll work directly with the Chief Client & Data Intelligence Officer as the strategist and operator at the center of a newly formed team. Your job is to keep decisions moving, teams connected and priority work getting finished, so the leadership team can focus on clients and growth.

It’s a role for someone who can shape a problem and then see it through. One week you might be building the business case for a new data product; the next you’re tightening the sales pipeline, preparing a board update and unblocking a delivery issue between product and engineering. You’ll move between sales enablement, product and data operations, and you’ll be trusted to run several projects at once without dropping any of them.

You’ll see the whole business, from client conversations to product decisions to the CEO’s agenda, and you’ll have influence over how a new organization works.

What you will do

Strategy and priority projects

  • Lead the organization’s highest-priority initiatives end to end, for example pricing, our investor program, entry into new markets and maturing the data strategy
  • Frame the problem, build the analysis, align stakeholders and drive the work through to a decision and implementation
  • Bring a recommendation, not just options

Operating rhythm and decision-making

  • Run the team’s operating cadence: weekly deal desk, fortnightly product council and monthly business review
  • Own the decision log, so it’s always clear what was decided, by whom and what happens next
  • Spot blockers between sales, product and data teams early and clear them

Commercial operations and sales enablement

  • Own pricing and support deal structuring with the sales team
  • Keep pipeline and ARR reporting accurate and trusted, with one view across GRESB
  • Work with sales and product to make sure the team has what it needs to showcase the value of the data products

Reporting and communication

  • Build and run the monthly CEO dashboard and KPI reporting
  • Prepare senior leadership, board and client materials that are clear, concise and decision-ready
  • Act as the Chief Client & Data Intelligence Officer’s point of contact when they’re away

What success looks like

In your first six months

  • The operating rhythm is running and people rely on it
  • The decision log is live and used
  • There’s one trusted ARR view across GRESB data products

By the end of your first year

  • At least two priority projects have been taken from problem to implemented decision
  • Leadership and board reporting runs on a predictable monthly cycle with little rework
  • Sales, product and data teams describe fewer handoff issues, and escalations get resolved faster

Requirements

  • Around 6–10 years of experience
  • A grounding in top-tier management consulting or Big Four advisory, in strategy, sustainability, data or technology
  • Ideally, spent time at a sustainability data, ESG ratings, real asset or financial data business
  • Strong business acumen and ability to work well in a cross-functional, global environment.
  • Experience implementing AI or advanced analytics solutions within a commercial or sales environment.
  • Proficiency in CRM, data analytics, and visualization tools.
  • A working understanding of how data products are packaged, priced and sold

How you work

  • You think in structure: you can break down an ambiguous problem, find what matters and build a clear path forward
  • You finish things. You run several projects at once and see each one through to the end
  • You’re organized, detail-oriented and work well in systems
  • You write and present clearly, whether it’s a one-page update or a board deck
  • You get things done without formal authority, by earning trust across sales, product and engineering
  • You’re comfortable moving between the big picture and the detail in the same day

Benefits

  • Involvement in a fast growing international data-driven company
  • Opportunity to work with a highly talented and committed team in a supportive environment with strong camaraderie
  • Annual leave of 25 days per calendar year
  • 2 volunteering days off per year
  • Company pension plan
  • Free public transport to and from the Amsterdam office
  • Free and healthy office lunch catered daily 
  • Annual professional development budget
  • Home office budget 

About GRESB

GRESB is the global sustainability intelligence standard for real assets. We transform sustainability data into decision-grade intelligence that drives capital allocation and asset improvement.

Our vision: An investment industry that plays a central role in creating a sustainable world.

Our mission: To provide financial markets with actionable sustainability insights, data, and benchmarks. More than 100 global institutional and financial investors rely on GRESB to help guide their investment decisions, mitigating risk, improving portfolio quality, and driving long-term financial success.

The GRESB team is an energetic group of more than 100 individuals from diverse backgrounds with experience spanning sustainability, data science, software development, real estate, infrastructure, and the capital markets. Most of us work out of our head office in Amsterdam or one of our satellite offices in London, Paris, Berlin, Boston, Singapore, or Sydney. We’re passionate about tackling the sustainability challenge by providing the insights that will power the markets of the future and enable investors to allocate the world’s capital in a more responsible way.

GRESB is a portfolio company of BeyondNetZero, General Atlantic's climate investing platform.

GRESB is an equitable, diverse, and inclusive workplace, one at which all workers - regardless of their gender, race, ethnicity, national origin, age, sexual orientation, identity, education, or disability - feel valued and respected. We are committed to a non-discriminatory approach to hiring and provide equal opportunity for employment and advancement in all of our teams and programs.

Ben jij een vooruitdenker die complexe data moeiteloos vertaalt naar glashelder advies? Neem jij van nature de regie, ben je sterk in stakeholdermanagement en heb je affiniteit met de dynamische wereld van Schiphol? Lees dan snel verder!

Binnen Orion Fleet Management zijn we op zoek naar een proactieve Senior Fleet Manager met een specifieke focus op onze klant Schiphol en ons label AirportPartners. Waar een reguliere Fleet Manager sterk leunt op de dagelijkse operatie, sta jij als Senior Fleet Manager daarboven. Jij kijkt verder dan de waan van de dag, anticipeert op wat komen gaat en gebruikt keiharde data om onze klant op strategisch niveau te adviseren.

Wat ga je doen?

In de rol van Senior Fleet Manager ben jij de absolute eigenaar van de vlootbeschikbaarheid voor Schiphol. Met ons label AirportPartners beheren wij hier de unieke en bedrijfskritische vloot van Schiphol: van de brandweerwagens en de onmisbare sneeuwvloot tot de personenwagens van het KLM-personeel. Jouw werk draait niet om achteraf reageren, maar om proactief sturen. Omdat jij de operationele basis feilloos begrijpt en beheerst, kun jij de vertaalslag maken naar optimalisatie en strategisch partnership. 

Jouw takenpakket als Senior Fleet Manager bestaat uit de volgende pijlers:

Datagedreven Regie & Strategie:

  • Proactieve advisering: Je wacht niet tot de klant belt met een probleem, maar je adviseert hen ongevraagd over rendementsverbetering en risicobeperking op basis van jouw data-analyses;

  • Datagedreven regie: Je gebruikt voorspellende data om de vloot optimaal in te zetten en stilstand te minimaliseren. Vooruitdenken is jouw tweede natuur;

  • Bewaking van SLA’s en KPI’s: Je monitort continu de prestaties, stuurt bij waar nodig en garandeert dat we onze beloftes aan de klant waarmaken (of overtreffen);

  • Rapportage en overleg: Je zit regelmatig aan tafel met het management van klanten en leveranciers. Je presenteert heldere rapportages en treedt op als een volwaardig en strategisch gesprekspartner.

Operationele Excellentie:

Om op strategisch niveau te kunnen adviseren, zorg jij dat de basisprocessen, de motor van de afdeling, vlekkeloos verlopen:

  • Triage en analyse: Je overziet de storingsmeldingen en zorgt voor een feilloze initiële beoordeling.

  • Slimme planning: Je overziet de planning van (preventief) onderhoud, altijd met de impact op de 24/7 luchthaven operatie en veiligheid op Schiphol in je achterhoofd;

  • Toetsing en beoordeling: Je beoordeelt complexe reparatie aanvragen kritisch op basis van historie, vastgelegde afspraken en toekomstige inzet van het voertuig;

Wat vragen we van jou?

Voor de rol van Senior Fleet Manager zoeken we iemand die stevig in zijn of haar schoenen staat. Je overziet het grote geheel, maar snapt de details die de data beïnvloeden. Verder zien wij graag het volgende terug:

  • Denkniveau: Je beschikt over HBO of WO werk- en denkniveau;

  • Sterk analytisch: Je bent een kei in het analyseren van data en haalt hier moeiteloos de juiste conclusies en actiepunten uit;

  • Proactieve mindset: Je wacht niet af, maar signaleert kansen en knelpunten voordat ze een probleem vormen;

  • Kennis & Ervaring: Je snapt hoe onderhoudsprocessen (triage, MTTR, MTBF) werken. Ervaring als Fleet Manager is een must en ervaring in de automotive of specifiek de OV-sector (bussen) is een zware pré;

  • Overtuigingskracht: Je hebt uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden. Je kunt draagvlak creëren en complexe technische of data-gerelateerde zaken begrijpelijk uitleggen aan directie, klanten en leveranciers.

Ben jij klaar voor deze stap als Senior Fleet Manager en wil je bouwen aan de toekomst van ons wagenparkbeheer op Schiphol? Druk dan snel op de sollicitatieknop en laat jouw cv en motivatie achter!

Wat bieden wij

Een leuke en uitdagende baan met veel zelfstandigheid en verantwoordelijkheid. Je komt te werken in een professionele en stabiele kantooromgeving. Orion is een sterk groeiend bedrijf binnen de Pon-onderneming en biedt doorgroeimogelijkheden in de toekomst.

Wat bieden we nog meer voor de functie van Senior Fleet Manager:

  • Een goed salaris tussen de € 4.579,- en € 6.538,- o.b.v. fulltime. Uiteraard is dit afhankelijk van jouw kennis en ervaring;

  • 28 vakantiedagen* en 6 ADV dagen;

  • Een individueel keuzebudget (o.a. te besteden voor het aankopen van verlof);

  • Directe en korte lijnen; je rapporteert rechtstreeks aan de Teamlead Operations;

  • De mogelijkheid om deels thuis te werken;

  • Een enthousiast, gezellig, compact en ambitieus team;

  • Een ruime Pon-pensioenregeling;

  • Een collectieve ziektekostenverzekering bij ONVZ of Zilveren Kruis waarbij Pon €300 per jaar bijdraagt;

  • Pon Fit: sportieve activiteiten waar je aan kan deelnemen! Van bootcamp tot golfclinic;

  • Korting op eigen producten van Pon (bijv. een nieuwe Gazelle fiets of privé lease auto), €500 per jaar;

  • Lease-a-bike regeling voor het leasen van een Pon-fiets.

Over de organisatie

Orion ontzorgt bedrijven met grote complexe wagenparken door het reparatie- en onderhoudsproces optimaal te structureren.

Binnen het netwerk heeft Orion een 15-tal eigen werkplaatsen onder de labels: AirportPartners, BusPartners en WastePartners. Onze werkplaatsen zijn gevestigd in: Almere, Amersfoort, Badhoevedorp-Schiphol (2 locaties), Ede, Emmeloord, Helmond, Leeuwarden, Leiden, Lichtenvoorde, Middelburg, Montfoort, Oosterwolde, Utrecht en Zwolle. Deze vacature is gericht op ons hoofdkantoor in Barneveld!

Met circa 250 collega’s zetten wij ons dagelijks in om ervoor te zorgen dat onder andere huis en bedrijfsafval opgehaald kunnen worden, vliegtuigen kunnen blijven opstijgen en landen en OV-reizigers in veilige en betrouwbare bussen kunnen reizen. Wij staan midden in de maatschappij en spelen in op trends als verstedelijking, elektrificatie, duurzaamheid en digitalisering. 

Iedereen is welkom !

Bij Orion en Pon maken de mensen het verschil. Wij geloven dat een diverse en inclusieve organisatie zorgt voor meer werkplezier, creativiteit en betere resultaten. Welke achtergrond, leeftijd of identiteit je ook meebrengt: als jij de motivatie en het talent hebt, horen we heel graag van je. 


Heb je vragen over de vacature of de sollicitatieprocedure? Neem gerust contact op met Wesley Bruinier (Recruiter) via +316 26 13 82 54 of .

About us

Hey there! We're Lleverage, and we're making the Autonomous Back Office actually achievable for businesses. We enable teams to capture, automate, and integrate AI agents into their business, because AI is only useful when it actually fits into daily operations. 

We help the most strategic European industries – manufacturing, logistics, and wholesale – automate the messy, manual processes that most tools can’t handle.

We’re a fast-growing, VC-backed scale-up based in Amsterdam, with big ambitions for 2026 and beyond. This is your chance to join early, have real impact, and grow alongside the company. If that sounds something you want to help build, we'd love to have you on board!

About the role

We're looking for an exceptional Go-To-Market Associate who will be the engine of our commercial team. As part of the top 1% of Commercial talents globally, you'll combine systematic prospecting with creative outreach to build relationships with decision-makers who need AI solutions.

This is not a classic sales role. We're looking for a builder with a commercial brain and an enormous drive, someone who combines hustle, strategic creativity, and genuine curiosity about what makes businesses tick.

You might come from a classic sales background, or you might have built your commercial instincts in a completely different arena. What matters far more than your CV is your drive, your entrepreneurial instinct, and the kind of work ethic that makes people wonder how you get so much done.

In a single day you might: map a new industry vertical for outreach opportunities, run a consultative discovery call with a Head of Operations at a manufacturing company, develop a proposal for a new channel, follow up on an active deal in scoping, and draft a business case for entering a completely new market.

You won't have a large team behind you. You will have full autonomy, meaningful equity, direct access to the founding team, and the freedom to experiment with what works.

Why Lleverage?

  • Change the world, literally: 2026 is the year AI works, and Lleverage.ai has the best AI platform (according to industry veterans)

  • Work, learn, have fun: You'll be part of a top-notch commercial team that operates at the highest level of performance

  • Build a unique network: Connect with decision-makers and operational leaders across traditional industries who are eager to implement AI solutions

  • Get autonomy & ownership: Design your own strategies and own your pipeline development

  • Compensation: We pay top of market cash and equity, with compensation tied to the pipeline value you create

Responsibilities

  • Own our top of funnel: which segments we go after, how we reach the COOs and CFOs of manufacturers and distributors, and how many qualified opportunities land in the pipeline every week. That's your number.

  • Sit in on live deals from day one: discovery calls, account plans, proposals and PoC scoping with our delivery team. Within 6 to 12 months you run your first deals yourself.

  • Build the playbook with the GTM lead and CCO: positioning per sector, messaging per persona, pricing experiments, the business cases we win with.

  • Run experiments across the whole funnel: outbound campaigns, events, partnerships with ERP partners and PE firms, LinkedIn content. Measure everything, scale what works.

  • Use AI-native tooling (Clay, lemlist, our own agents) to research, personalise and scale what a team of five used to do by hand, and help us figure out what GTM looks like when AI does the grunt work.

  • Bring what you see in the market to the founding team and product: which use cases, sectors, competitors and prices we should bet on next.


Job specific requirements

  • 1 to 3 years in consulting, investment banking, PE or a fast-growing B2B startup, or you built something yourself.

  • You make things happen without a brief, and can show it with an example and a number.

  • You win trust fast, with a CFO in a boardroom and with an operations manager on a factory floor.

  • You think in funnels and business cases and turn data into a clear recommendation.

  • New sectors, no playbook, channels nobody has tried: that energises you rather than stops you. A no on Monday doesn't define your Tuesday.

  • Genuinely curious about how businesses make money and where they lose it.

  • You want to own revenue within a year and know why.

  • Fluent Dutch and English, German is a big plus

Nice to haves

  • Worked with or for manufacturing, wholesale, logistics or food companies.

  • Hands-on with HubSpot, Clay or lemlist.

  • Understanding of ERP-driven processes (SAP, Business Central, Exact).

  • Sold something before: side business, campus sales, fundraising.

Our Tech Stack

You'll be working with best-in-class tools:

  • CRM: HubSpot for pipeline management

  • Prospecting: AI-powered research and outreach tools like Clay and Lemlist

  • Communication: Multi-channel outreach across email, LinkedIn, and phone

  • Analytics: Data-driven insights to optimize your approach

  • And always exploring what's next

We offer

You are ready for the ride of a lifetime with experienced entrepreneurs and innovators who aim for hyper growth on a global scale. We look for an enormous drive and hands-on mentality. Somebody who can work with us in creating the best AI platform out there!

We offer a good salary, a highly experienced (and very entertaining...) team and considerable share and bonus packages. And last but not least, this is the start of your career to grow to into a commercial lead and to lay the foundation for years to come.

Jouw impact bij Movares

Met jouw ecologische expertise geef je richting aan de bescherming en versterking van natuur binnen uiteenlopende projecten. Je borgt kwaliteit, brengt ecologie strategisch in en zorgt dat natuur volwaardig wordt meegenomen in ontwerp- en besluitvorming.

Dit ga je doen bij Movares

  • je werkt aan complexe adviestrajecten op het gebied van natuurwetgeving, ecologisch onderzoek en vergunningverlening. Je schakelt intensief met verschillende stakeholders en bent van begin tot eind betrokken bij projecten. Je adviseert over vraagstukken rondom beschermde gebieden (waaronder stikstof), houtopstanden en (zeldzame) beschermde soorten, zoals zandhagedis, rugstreeppad, vuursalamander, das en bever;

  • een belangrijk onderdeel van je rol is het begeleiden van junioren en medioren. Je ondersteunt hen in projecten, bespreekt resultaten, bewaakt de kwaliteit van rapportages en stimuleert hun inhoudelijke groei. Je draagt bij aan de verdere opbouw van kennis in het team en helpt om ecologie stevig te verankeren binnen integrale projectteams;

  • de projecten waar je aan werkt zijn divers: van damwandvervanging in stedelijke parken tot spoorvernieuwingen door het hele land en de renovatie van bruggen in grote steden. Jij brengt ecologie op een natuurlijke manier in als volwaardig onderdeel van het ontwerp- en besluitvormingsproces. Daarnaast kijk je altijd verder dan de wettelijke eisen en onderzoek je hoe projecten extra natuurwaarde kunnen creëren. Dat vertaal je naar concrete maatregelen, zoals faunapassages, wadi’s of groene gevels;

  • rapportages, ecologische beoordelingen en stikstofonderbouwingen behoren tot je vaste werkzaamheden. Je speelt een belangrijke rol in de kwaliteitsborging binnen het team en binnen de projecten waarin je meedraait;

  • in het zuiden van het land liggen voor de ecologen van Movares volop kansen. Daarom breiden we het team uit. Jij vervult daarin een trekkersrol. Naast je inhoudelijke adviseurschap geef je leiding aan een klein team van ecologen. Je stimuleert hun ontwikkeling en bewaakt planning en kwaliteit. Ook bouw je actief aan relaties met klanten en partners in de regio.

Dit ben jij bij Movares

Als senior adviseur breng je visie, ervaring en vakinhoudelijke kracht mee. Je bent gewend om zelfstandig te opereren in complexe projecten en weet wat nodig is om tot goed onderbouwde, uitvoerbare adviezen te komen. Je vindt het vanzelfsprekend om collega’s te helpen in hun ontwikkeling en hebt oog voor de kwaliteit van het totale ecologische product dat we als team leveren.

Dit breng je ook mee:

  • een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding in (toegepaste) Biologie, Bos- en Natuurbeheer, Ecologie of vergelijkbaar;

  • vanaf 8 jaar ervaring als ecologisch adviseur of ecoloog;

  • uitstekende kennis van natuurwetgeving en natuurbeleid.

Dit krijg je bij Movares

Bij Movares werk je aan opgaven die Nederland verder helpen. Tegelijk krijg je de ruimte om je werk en loopbaan in te richten op een manier die bij jou past. Met goede arbeidsvoorwaarden, veel flexibiliteit en volop mogelijkheden om je te ontwikkelen.

Een sterk fundament

Een goede basis begint bij voorwaarden waarop je kunt rekenen:

• een salaris tussen € 5.500 en € 7.500 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur;

• een flexibele pot van minimaal 15% van je jaarsalaris, inclusief vakantiegeld;

• een goede pensioenregeling bij Zwitserleven, waarbij Movares twee derde van de pensioenpremie betaalt;

• een NS Business Card voor woon-werkverkeer en zakelijke reizen. Privé profiteer je met de kaart van de dalurenkorting.

Maximaal flexibel

Vorm een manier van werken die aansluit bij jouw leven én jouw ambities. Maak keuzes die bij jou passen:

• flexibel werken volgens ons Any Time Any Place-principe, passend bij je team, klanten en projecten;

• de mogelijkheid om twee weken per jaar te werken vanaf je vakantieadres binnen de EU;

• 20 vakantiedagen bij een fulltime dienstverband, met de mogelijkheid om extra dagen te kopen vanuit je flexibele pot;

• met je flexibele pot kies je wat voor jou belangrijk is, bijvoorbeeld voor extra inkomen, pensioen, een fiets, bedrijfsfitness, verduurzaming van je woning of het aflossen van je studieschuld;

• € 750 budget per vijf jaar om je thuiswerkplek goed in te richten;

• € 2,45 netto thuiswerkvergoeding per thuiswerkdag.

Veel ontwikkelmogelijkheden

Ontwikkel een loopbaan die past bij jouw talenten en ambities. Kies jouw eigen pad:

• ruimte om je expertise, ambitie en loopbaan verder te ontwikkelen;

• leren door te doen, samen met ervaren collega's en met gebruik van een breed aanbod aan ontwikkelmogelijkheden;

• de kans om actief kennis te delen en mee te bouwen aan de toekomst van ons vakgebied.

Samen groeien

Deel mee in de waarde die we samen creëren en de groei van onze organisatie. Samen voor succes:

• je flexibele pot groeit mee met de resultaten van Movares;

• een winstdeling met een doelbedrag van 5% van je bruto jaarsalaris, afhankelijk van de resultaten;

• en de mogelijkheid tot participeren in de waardeontwikkeling van Movares door middel van aankoop van phantom aandelen.

Jouw team bij Movares

Je maakt deel uit van het team Ecologie binnen de marktunit Planvorming & Conditionering. Dit team verbindt omgeving, natuur en projectbelangen op een zorgvuldige en inhoudelijk sterke manier. Je werkt samen met collega’s met expertise in onder meer ecologie, waterkwaliteit, klimaatadaptatie, GIS, vergunningen, omgevingsmanagement, bodem en milieu.

Samen zorgen jullie ervoor dat projecten uitvoerbaar zijn én meerwaarde creëren voor natuur. Door disciplines te verbinden ontstaan integrale, realistische en toekomstbestendige oplossingen. Binnen het team is veel samenwerking en kennisdeling, met ruimte voor hybride werken en aandacht voor een prettige balans tussen werk en collegiaal contact.

Jouw team bij Movares

Je werkt samen met een hechte groep geotechnische adviseurs die elkaar makkelijk weten te vinden. Eén dag per week – op woensdag – werken jullie sowieso samen op kantoor in Utrecht. Daarnaast is twee dagen per week op kantoor gangbaar, maar stemmen we locatie en werktijden flexibel af. Er is altijd iemand aanwezig en de lijnen zijn kort.

De sfeer in het team is open en gelijkwaardig. Er is weinig hiërarchie: senioriteit gaat hier niet over ‘boven iemand staan’, maar over kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Collega’s kunnen goed met elkaar opschieten, schakelen snel en staan voor elkaar klaar. Samenwerken doen we bewust, omdat we geloven dat je daar betere oplossingen van maakt.
